newsitem.title: CANADA: BASEBALL-KEVIN YOUNG SLAM RALLIES PIRATES PAST EXPOS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-KEVIN YOUNG SLAM RALLIES PIRATES PAST EXPOS.

text.p: In a game that saw four home runs, Kevin Young's first career grand slam was the big blow, capping a five-run eighth inning to rally the Pittsburgh Pirates past the Montreal Expos 8-6 Sunday.
Young drove the first pitch from Expos' reliever Lee Smith over the centre field wall to give Pittsburgh an 8-4 lead.
"I have a lot of respect for Lee Smith, he's a great ambassador of the game," said Young. "That alone makes it a special moment for me.

Mark Wilkins (4-0) allowed a run and a hit in relief of Pirates' starter Esteban Loaiza to pick up the win. Rich Loiselle tossed a scoreless ninth inning for his fourth save, as the Pirates won for just the third time in nine games.
Omar Daal (1-1) gave up two runs and a hit while retiring two batters as Montreal used seven pitchers in the game.
The Pirates trailed 2-0 until Dale Sveum hit a three-run homer off Montreal starter Dustin Hermanson in the fifth. It was Sveum's first homer of the season, and just his second since 1994.
"The guy took me deep, that's the name of the game," said Hermanson. "One pitch can change the whole outcome of the game, that's what happened today."
Mike Lansing hit two home runs, both solo shots, for the second time this season for the Expos, who lost for only the third time in their last 10 home games.
At Colorado, Ellis Burks homered for the fifth time in six games and Dante Bichette added three singles as the Rockies beat the Houston Astros 8-5.
Colorado erased an early 4-0 deficit and improved to 18-4 all-time against Houston at Coors Field.
Burks, who had three hits and two RBI, drove a 3-1 offering from John Hudek 421 feet over the left-field wall in the eighth inning, giving the Rockies a 7-5 lead.
Burks and Bichette, hitting second and third in the lineup, were on base a combined eight times.

In Los Angeles, Ismael Valdes, Darren Hall and Todd Worrell outdueled Denny Neagle, combining on a three-hitter to send him to his first loss of the season, as the Dodgers held on for a 2-0 victory over the Atlanta Braves.

Valdes (3-5) allowed three hits over seven innings, walking none with six strikeouts. Hall worked a perfect eighth, striking out two. Worrell held the Braves off the board in the ninth for his 13th save in 16 chances.
Todd Zeile and Billy Ashley singled in the seventh to put the Dodgers up 1-0 and Mike Piazza doubled in Raul Mondesi, who had walked, to make it 2-0 in the eighth.
Neagle (7-1) allowed both runs and six hits with four walks and five strikeouts in 7 1/3 innings.
In Cincinnati, Bret Boone's sacrifice fly brought home the go-ahead run in a four-run fifth inning that helped the Reds to a 7-5 victory over the Chicago Cubs.

Pete Schourek (3-4) earned the victory despite allowing three home runs for the second straight game. He gave up four runs and five hits with a walk, three strikeouts and two hit batsmen in five innings. Reds pitchers lead the league with 29 hit batsmen. Kent Bottenfield (1-1) took the loss.
Doug Glanville, Scott Servais and Jose Hernandez had the Cincinnati homers.
In San Diego, Kevin Brown scattered 12 hits and Bobby Bonilla homered and drove in three runs as the Florida Marlins beat the Padres 6-2.
Brown (5-2) struck out eight without a walk as he went all the way for the second time this season. He retired the side in order just twice and was helped by two double plays.
Bonilla had an RBI single in a three-run first and hit a two-run homer in the eighth, just his second of the season. He lifted his average to .327 with 26 RBI.
After winning five in a row, San Diego has dropped two straight and remains in last place in the Western Division.

In San Francisco, Ray Lankford's two-run single snapped a tie in the third inning and Delino DeShields had a two-run triple to cap a five-run fifth inning as the St Louis Cardinals defeated the Giants 9-3.
Todd Stottlemyre (3-3) allowed three runs and six hits in seven innings en route to his 100th career victory. He had three walks and a season-high eight strikeouts.
Marcus Jensen hit his first major-league homer, a two-run shot in the second, for the Giants.
In Philadelphia, the scheduled game between the New York Mets and Phillies at Veterans Stadium was postponed due to rain. It will be made up as part of a doubleheader on Monday, September 15.
